navigation.explode: Discover the impacts of farmed salmon

impact.title: Every year in France,
impact.description: Almost all the salmon we eat in France comes from fish farms. They are not caught in the wild. They are fed every day for two years in cages.

menuCards.title: Wild fish turned into fishmeal and fish oil
menuCards.content: Salmon are carnivorous fish. In fish farming, 440 small wild fish are caught and processed into fishmeal and fish oil to feed just 1 salmon. This fishing causes "accidental" catches of sharks, turtles, whales…

menuCards.title: Soy, wheat and rapeseed
menuCards.content: Salmon are carnivorous fish, yes... but they are also fed soy, wheat and rapeseed. Demand for soy for farmed animals is a driver of both legal and illegal deforestation in Brazil.

menuCards.title: Krill caught in Antarctica
menuCards.content: To enhance its pink color, salmon are also fed krill, tiny shrimp that serve as food for many animals in the Antarctic ecosystem.

menuCards.title: Antiparasitic treatments
menuCards.content: Cages encourage infections. Industrial fish farmers administer antiparasitic treatments, mainly against sea lice, a type of marine tick that attaches itself to salmon skin.

menuCards.title: Microplastics
menuCards.content: Farmed salmon can ingest microplastics present in their environment or feed.

menuCards.title: Forever chemicals
menuCards.content: Feed used in aquaculture can expose fish to PFAS, PCBs and dioxins.

title.part1: In France, each person consumes an average of 4.5 kg of farmed salmon per year,

results.intro: The total (for the entire French population) comes to:

item1.title: 62 million salmon
item1.description: killed every year, each spending 2 years confined and crammed together, fed on pellets

item2.title: 27 billion small fish
item2.description: killed every year, caught specifically to produce the fishmeal and fish oil used to feed salmon, affecting local populations in West Africa

item3.title: 128,000 tonnes of nitrogen and phosphorus discharged
item3.description: by fish farms through salmon waste, uneaten feed, treatment residues, etc.

item4.title: 1.9 million tonnes of CO2
item4.description: generated every year, equivalent to the annual emissions of 235,000 people in France

item1.title: 987 km² of land are used
item1.description: to produce plant-based feed for salmon. That's more than the combined area of Seine-Saint-Denis, Hauts-de-Seine and Paris.

item2.title: 12 persistent organic pollutants (POPs)
item2.description: found in salmon. Of the dozen pollutants listed under the Stockholm Convention, all twelve are found in salmon.

item3.title: Less omega-3
item3.description: Today, salmon flesh contains significantly less omega-3 than it used to. This is a consequence of changes in the feed given to salmon.
